comment: The shelved ion's telegraph as the characterising experiment of the click's round (the owner's word of 2026-10-02, about 11:00 Israel, 'Yes to the experiment', on the Boss's proposal of 10:50; HIGHLIGHTS.md, the lines of 10:48, 11:00 and 11:20; the two hands' design: the mathematician's 138, #1572 comment 5947659375, the telegraph as three clicks under the owner's line of 131 to 137, and the advisor's blind, #1572 comment 5947666040 section 4, corrected by his 5948063089 section 1, the shelving rate Zeno-limited; nature: Bergquist, Hulet, Itano and Wineland 1986, the telegraph of one Hg+ ion, 30 or 0 counts per 10 ms with the dark mean 0.09 s, and Itano, Heinzen, Bollinger and Wineland 1990, the Zeno-limited rate). Every number of the two worlds and of the blind stands in this file; the engine reads none of it. The folder holds the universe file `mercury_ion.json`, the world `shelved_ion.json`, its control `shelved_ion_control.json` and the blind `expectation.json`, written before any lay and any run, and no builder: the world is laid by no generator of main (status below) and the files were written by hand from this design, every key a declaration. TWO HYPOTHESES OF THE TEST WORLD UNDER THEIR OWN NAMES, declarations of the files and nothing in the engine (the owner's word of 11:00): (1) THE MODES AS LABELS (the mathematician's 124, declaration 1, #1572 comment 5946705567): the ion's family has the parts shape [3, 2], three planes laid as one event and never summed at a Node, the part the body's label, S (the ground mode), P (the excited mode the strong drive feeds) and D (the metastable shelf the weak drive feeds); the three shapes are laid by the file at interval 0 (the `parts` key of the body, S with the count 1, P and D with 0), the parts sharing one pair and so one rest rotation, so that the energy of a transition is not the board's and the quantum a part gives is laid at the frequency of the drive that fed the transition (the lay's balance per branch, 126 (2): the given light's frequency is the drive's); the atom's spectrum is not solved by the labels (124, what it does not solve) and this world asks nothing of it. (2) THE GIVING AT A DECLARED RATE (the mathematician's 126 (1), the floor; 128 B, 'a fifth act under its own name'; the owner's decision of 10:20 and his word of 10:20 on the Node level, HIGHLIGHTS.md): a quantum standing in an excited part is given to the light at the declared rate 1 / lifetime per interval (the `rates` key of the body), the exponential by construction and the rate one number read from nature until a derivation; the fluorescence P -> S at 1 / tau_P and the return D -> S at 1 / tau_D. THE BODY AS A NODEDETECTOR (the act of branch click-ends, the advisor's form at the owner's word of 10:20, two hands with 138): the body absorbs a quantum of a drive at the two-mode line's share and is re-laid in the realised part over its own Nodes with its whole count, the other parts 0 there (the shelving: the weak drive's quantum taken, the ion re-laid in D); it emits a quantum at the declared rate, laying one whole quantum of light at its shell Node on the row the body names (`gives_to`) and re-laying itself in the lower part (the fluorescence: P -> S, the light on the row `fluorescence`; the return: D -> S, the light on the weak drive's own row, the frequency the drive's); every draw with the file's seed, the run deterministic per seed. THE WORLD: a periodic box of 12 x 12 x 7 Nodes on the universe `mercury_ion.json` (no holder of the content, as the nuclide's universe: the ion is one quantum and its content well is nothing); the ion one quantum of the family `ion` at the near-flat pair [1, 1299] (the toy atom's heavy family on branch toy-worlds, cos omega = 1 / 1299, the band's inertia m* = 3 tan omega = 3,897: nature's ion is 200 times a nucleon and held by its trap; here it is held by its inertia and re-laid at its declared Nodes at every click, spreading between clicks by t / (2 m*), 0.21 Links over the longest dark period) at the two centre Nodes [6, 6, 4] and [7, 6, 4], its shell Nodes themselves; two drives as two holders of the sign under the act `rotation` (ALGEBRA.md, The sign holder rotates the two-part record; The turn per proper interval), each a plane wave of its own row laid by the packet lay over the whole box on a periodic axis, so that it circulates for the whole run with its amplitude at the ion constant: `strong_drive` along x at k = pi / 2 and the amplitude 3,000, the S <-> P drive, saturating, and `weak_drive` along y at k = pi / 2 and the amplitude 53, the S -> D drive; a third holder of the sign, `fluorescence`, carrying no drive, on which the P -> S quantum is laid, so that the counter reads the fluorescence apart from the drives (a counter reading the drive's own row would write its hole into the drive at every click); one counter, `fluorescence_counter`, every Node of the box but the ion's two, so that every given quantum enters it within a few intervals through the ion's two Nodes' ten outer Ports (nature's counter sees a solid angle of about 10^-4 of the fluorescence; here the whole of it, and the counts per bin are the quanta given per bin), with the `draw` key as branch click-ends declares it (the window B = 160 intervals, the seed 24, the generator x <- (multiplier x + increment) mod 2^width with the gate worlds' two integers and the width the universe file's 63); no face recedes: a drain by a receding face grows the board at light's pace, 0.45 Links per interval at k = pi / 2, and ends the run at the axis's largest size within a few hundred intervals of a run of 96,000, so the box is periodic and a emitted quantum, once credited (the count down by one in the credit's accounting, the levels at one Node taken), stays on the board as an empty wave, uncreditable, its share at the ion's Node at most the accumulated share over the box's 1,008 Nodes (`fence`). THE BLIND in the law's names (expectation.json, written before any run): the fluorescence rate R = 1 / (2 tau_P) per interval under the saturating strong drive (the P part's mean share one half), so the counts per bin of B intervals in a bright period are Poisson with the mean B / (2 tau_P) = 20; the shelving rate Zeno-limited, Omega_w^2 / R, with Omega_w the weak drive's Rabi rate in the law's units, k_r ell_w / Gamma times the two modes' overlap (the weak light's level at the body, 53, over Gamma, the read weight 1 and the overlap 1 since the parts' shapes are alike), so the bright periods are exponential with the mean R / Omega_w^2 = 1,602 intervals; the return at 1 / tau_D, the dark periods exponential with the mean tau_D = 1,600; the dark fraction tau_D / (tau_D + R / Omega_w^2) = 0.4997; the counts per bin BIMODAL, two peaks, at 20 and at 0; the control, the same world on today's engine with no draw and no body's click, unimodal (0 in every bin: a steady rotation writes no beat and no quantum is given without the act; the law as written before the write, the emission drawn from the shares without the re-lay, 128's verdict, unimodal Poisson at the mean rate). The ratios kept: tau_P much less than B (4 against 160), B much less than tau_D and than R / Omega_w^2 (160 against 1,600), tau_D about R / Omega_w^2 (1,600 against 1,602), the run 30 (tau_D + R / Omega_w^2) = 96,000 intervals, 600 bins, about 30 switches; the bin over the dark mean 0.10 as nature's 10 ms over 90 ms. Laid by the generator (the mode files beside the worlds), admitted by the loader; run once at the frozen hash by the experimenter against this blind.

worlds.shelved_ion: the telegraph world, read by this blind's rows 1 to 7

rule: the counter's `credit` lines of the family `fluorescence` (branch click-ends: one line per credited quantum, with its window), counted per window of B intervals, are the counts per bin; a bin with 0 counts is dark and a bin with 1 or more is bright (Poisson at the mean 20 gives 0 with the probability 2 x 10^-9, so no bright bin reads 0 and the two kinds are told apart by the count alone); a run of bright bins between two dark ones is a bright period and a run of dark bins a dark period, their lengths in bins times B in intervals, the first and the last period dropped as cut by the window; the counter's `credit` lines of the family `weak_drive` are the returns, one per dark period's end; `click` lines are the inflows per interval, read by no row (the drives' net inflow 0 but for the rounding, the fluorescence's the quanta's passage), and `field` lines, the books and every array are lattice readings

nature.Bergquist_Hulet_Itano_Wineland_1986: Phys. Rev. Lett. 57, 1699: one Hg+ ion, the 194 nm S-P fluorescence under a saturating drive, the 282 nm S-D weak drive, 30 or 0 counts per 10 ms bin, bright and dark periods, tau_D = 0.09 s
nature.Itano_Heinzen_Bollinger_Wineland_1990: Phys. Rev. A 41, 2295: the quantum Zeno effect, the weak transition's rate limited by the strong transition's resets, Omega_w^2 / R in form
nature.Cook_Kimble_1985: Phys. Rev. Lett. 54, 1023: the telegraph's statistics from rate equations, exponential periods
nature.scaling: the engine's intervals compress nature's: tau_P / B is 2.3 x 10^-7 in nature and 0.025 here; B / tau_D 0.11 and 0.10

status_of_the_worlds: laid by the generator (the mode files beside the worlds), admitted by the loader; run once at the frozen hash by the experimenter against this blind

1_bright_bins_poisson.reading: the counts per bin over the bright bins of `shelved_ion` (the rule above), their mean and their variance
1_bright_bins_poisson.blind: Poisson with the mean B / (2 tau_P) = 20 counts per bin, the variance the mean, 20 +/- 4.5 per bin
1_bright_bins_poisson.status: computed from the law's names: the P -> S emission at the declared rate 1 / tau_P from the P part's share, the P part's mean share one half under the saturating strong drive (the two-mode line), so R = 1 / (2 tau_P) per interval and B R = 20 per bin (the advisor's 5947666040 section 4, row 1); at the declared level 3,000 the two-mode line's saturation s = 2 (Omega_s tau_P)^2 = 8 gives the P share 0.444 and 17.8 per bin, the finite-saturation number beside the saturated one
1_bright_bins_poisson.fence: clicks; the bins' width beside the Poisson's: the empty waves accumulated on the fluorescence row (the emitted quanta after their credit, up to about 6,000 over 1,008 Nodes) hold at the ion's Node a share of at most about 6 quanta by the run's end, whose change per window enters the counter's inflow as noise of that order, a lattice matter

2_bright_periods_exponential.reading: the bright periods' lengths in intervals (bins times B), their mean, and their distribution's shape (the standard deviation over the mean, 1 for an exponential)
2_bright_periods_exponential.blind: exponential with the mean R / Omega_w^2 = 1602 intervals (10.0 bins)
2_bright_periods_exponential.status: computed from the law's names: the shelving is the body's absorption click of the weak drive's quantum into D at the two-mode line's share, which builds coherently as (Omega_w t)^2 between resets and is reset by every fluorescence click re-laying the ion in S, so the share per fluorescence interval is (Omega_w / R)^2 and the shelving rate is Omega_w^2 / R, the Zeno-limited rate (the mathematician's 138; the advisor's 5948063089 section 1, correcting his 5947666040 section 4's incoherent Phi_w / W_c; Itano 1990), with Omega_w = k_r ell_w / Gamma x overlap = 53 / 6000; the same lines with the resets' waiting times exponential at the rate R give 2 Omega_w^2 / R and the mean 801, the hands' number kept as the blind and the factor named

3_dark_periods_exponential.reading: the dark periods' lengths in intervals, their mean and their distribution's shape
3_dark_periods_exponential.blind: exponential with the mean tau_D = 1600 intervals (10 bins)
3_dark_periods_exponential.status: a declaration's consequence: the return D -> S is the emission click at the declared rate 1 / tau_D per interval (126 (1), the floor), exponential by construction; nature's tau_D = 0.09 s against the 10 ms bin (Bergquist 1986), the ratio 0.11 against this world's 0.10

4_dark_fraction.reading: the dark bins over all the bins of the window
4_dark_fraction.status: computed from rows 2 and 3, the two means equal by the choice of the integers (the advisor's 5947666040 section 4, row 4)

5_bimodal.reading: the histogram of the counts per bin over the window
5_bimodal.blind: two peaks, at 20 (Poisson width) and at 0, about 300 bins each, and nothing between but the Poisson's tail (the probability of a bright bin under 8 is 0.002)
5_bimodal.status: the telegraph's statistic from rows 1 and 4 (the advisor's 5947666040 section 4, row 5; Bergquist 1986, 30 or 0 counts per 10 ms); the one click of nature the law as written FAILED (128) and the hypotheses of the test world meet or fail by name

6_switches.reading: the number of bright periods and of dark periods in the window
6_switches.blind: about 30 of each, the run being 30 (tau_D + R / Omega_w^2) intervals

7_returns.reading: the counter's `credit` lines of the family `weak_drive` over the window, and the bins they fall in
7_returns.blind: one per dark period, in the last dark bin of the period or the first bright one after it, about 30 in all; none of the family `strong_drive`
7_returns.status: a consequence of the declarations: the return D -> S lays one quantum on the weak drive's row at the shell Node (`gives_to`), which the counter credits as it credits the fluorescence; the drives' plane waves give the counter a net inflow of 0 but for the rounding, so the strong drive is credited never and the weak drive only at a return

8_control_unimodal.reading: the counts per bin of `shelved_ion_control`, the same world on today's engine with no draw and no body's click, once its body can be laid
8_control_unimodal.blind: 0 in every bin, one peak at 0, unimodal: no quantum is given without the emission click (a steady rotation writes no beat and the parts share one rotation), the fluorescence row stays at its static rest and the counter has nothing to credit
8_control_unimodal.status: derived from the law as written (ALGEBRA.md, no spontaneous click; HIGHLIGHTS.md, 128's verdict); the intermediate control the advisor names, the emission drawn from the shares without the body's re-lay, gives a Poisson sequence unimodal at the mean rate times the bright fraction and no dark period, a world no branch lays

9_the_ion_stands.reading: the ion family's share at its Node and over the board at every interval (Lattice.share_of), the parts' counts, and the counter's `credit` lines of the family `ion`
9_the_ion_stands.blind: the ion's count 1 at every interval, one part at 1 and two at 0 after every click, its share at its Node above 0.9 of a quantum between clicks (the spread t / (2 m*) at m* = 3,897, 0.21 Links over the longest dark period), and no `credit` line of the family `ion` (its share entering the counter per window under 10^-3 of a quantum)
9_the_ion_stands.status: computed from the near-flat pair's inertia and the re-lay at the declared Node; the counter's credit rounds its window inflow to the nearest whole quantum
9_the_ion_stands.fence: lattice for the shares; clicks for the absence of an ion credit

10_the_drives_stand.reading: the drives' levels at the ion's Node over the run and the counter's `click` lines of the families `strong_drive` and `weak_drive` summed per window
10_the_drives_stand.blind: the strong drive's amplitude at the ion 3,000 within 2 percent over the run (about 6,000 quanta taken of 210,000) and the weak drive's 53 within 2 percent (about 30 taken of 66, each absorption the levels at one Node, 0.06 of a quantum); the net window inflow of either drive into the counter 0 but for the rounding and the fresh return
10_the_drives_stand.status: computed from the plane waves' uniform and constant share on the periodic axes and from the counts of the design
10_the_drives_stand.fence: lattice for the levels; clicks for the inflows
